Job Description: Accounts & Finance Manager (Chartered Accountant)

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Chartered Accountant to lead our Finance & Accounts function. The Accounts & Finance Manager will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of accounting, financial reporting, taxation, budgeting, treasury, statutory compliance, audits, and internal controls. The role requires strong analytical abilities, leadership skills, and a strategic mindset to support business growth while ensuring compliance with all applicable financial and regulatory requirements.

The ideal candidate should possess extensive knowledge of Indian accounting standards, direct and indirect taxation, financial planning and analysis, ERP systems, and corporate governance. The candidate will work closely with senior management to drive financial efficiency, improve business performance, and support strategic decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Accounting & Reporting

- Manage the complete accounting function and ensure accurate recording of all financial transactions.
- Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in compliance with applicable accounting standards.
- Ensure timely book closure and preparation of trial balance, profit & loss account, balance sheet, and cash flow statements.
- Review general ledger balances and perform account reconciliations.
- Monitor fixed assets, depreciation schedules, and capital expenditure accounting.
- Ensure timely month-end and year-end closing activities.

2. Taxation & Statutory Compliance

- Ensure complete compliance with GST, TDS, Income Tax, Professional Tax, and other applicable statutory regulations.
- Review and file GST returns, TDS returns, Income Tax returns, and other statutory filings within prescribed timelines.
- Handle tax assessments, departmental notices, and litigation support.
- Coordinate with tax consultants and legal advisors for compliance and advisory matters.
- Monitor changes in tax laws and assess their impact on the organization.
- Ensure timely payment of statutory dues and maintain proper documentation.

3. Audit & Internal Controls

- Lead statutory audits, internal audits, tax audits, and cost audits.
- Coordinate with external auditors and ensure timely completion of audits.
- Implement recommendations arising from audit findings.
- Develop and strengthen internal financial controls and SOPs.
- Ensure compliance with company policies and statutory requirements.
- Conduct periodic financial risk assessments and recommend mitigation measures.

4. Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Planning

- Prepare annual operating budgets in consultation with department heads.
- Develop monthly and quarterly financial forecasts.
- Analyze budget versus actual performance and provide variance analysis.
- Support strategic financial planning and long-term business forecasting.
- Recommend cost optimization and profitability improvement initiatives.

5. Treasury & Cash Flow Management

- Monitor daily cash flow and liquidity requirements.
- Manage banking relationships and oversee fund management activities.
- Prepare cash flow forecasts and optimize working capital.
- Coordinate loan documentation, banking facilities, and financial instruments.
- Ensure efficient utilization of available funds.

6. MIS & Financial Analysis

- Prepare monthly MIS reports for senior management.
- Develop dashboards and KPI reports for business performance monitoring.
- Analyze profitability, margins, operating costs, and financial trends.
- Present financial insights to support strategic decision-making.
- Identify opportunities for revenue enhancement and cost reduction.

7. Accounts Payable & Receivable

- Monitor vendor payments and ensure timely settlement.
- Review customer receivables and coordinate collection activities.
- Ensure proper reconciliation of customer and vendor accounts.
- Improve receivable cycles and reduce outstanding balances.

8. ERP & Process Improvement

- Ensure effective utilization of ERP systems for finance operations.
- Participate in ERP implementation, upgrades, and process automation initiatives.
- Improve accounting processes through digitization and automation.
- Develop standardized financial procedures across business functions.

9. Team Management

- Lead, supervise, and mentor the finance and accounts team.
- Allocate responsibilities and monitor team performance.
- Conduct regular performance reviews and training sessions.
- Foster a culture of accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvement.

10. Business Support

- Provide financial support for new projects, investments, and expansion initiatives.
- Conduct financial feasibility studies and investment analysis.
- Support management during mergers, acquisitions, fundraising, or due diligence activities.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve operational efficiency.

Required Qualifications

- Chartered Accountant (CA) qualification is mandatory.
- Bachelor's degree in Commerce, Finance, or Accounting.
- 7+ years of post-qualification experience in accounting, finance, taxation, and audit.
- Experience in manufacturing, engineering, FMCG, retail, or service industries will be an advantage.

Technical Skills

- Solid knowledge of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and financial reporting.
- Thorough understanding of GST, Income Tax, TDS, Companies Act, and other statutory regulations.
- Hands-on experience with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Tally Prime, or similar platforms.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including Pivot Tables, Power Query, Lookup functions, dashboards, and financial modeling.
- Experience in budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and variance analysis.
- Knowledge of internal controls, audit processes, and risk management.

Job Types: Full-time, Permanent

Pay: ₹20,000.00 - ₹80,000.00 per month

Work Location: In person

Candidate Requirements

Experience

Skills & Competencies
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Good knowledge of accounting principles, auditing standards, and regulatory compliance.
• Proficiency in MS Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; knowledge of audit tools preferred.
• Ability to work under deadlines, manage multiple assignments, and adapt to dynamic work environments.
• Strong communication and report writing skills.
• Ethical, detail-oriented, and a team player.

What You'll Do

Avalara is seeking a detail-oriented Financial Instruments Accounting Lead with deep expertise across debt, investment, trust, treasury, and derivative accounting — and a genuine drive to leverage AI and automation to transform accounting processes and enhance insights. This role owns the accuracy, integrity, and completeness of all financial instruments-related balances, journal entries, and public-company-style disclosures within Avalara's consolidated financial statements.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Debt Accounting
• Prepare, post, and self-review journal entries for term loans, revolving credit, and borrowings (ASC 470) with audit-ready documentation.
• Maintain and reconcile debt schedules (principal, issuance costs, discount/premium); apply the effective interest method and ensure accuracy of interest expense and accruals at each period-end.
• Support debt disclosures for mock 10-Q/10-K filings
• Monitor debt covenant requirements — including lender EBITDA definitions and compliance calculations

Investment Accounting
• Account for the investment portfolio (Cash Equivalent, Short Term & Long-term Investments) under ASC 320, 321, 323 and 325— ensuring proper classification, recognition, and measurement across trading, available-for-sale, held-to-maturity and other investment categories; support disclosures for mock 10-Q/10-K filings.
• Perform mark-to-market or amortized cost calculations as applicable and ensure proper balance sheet classification and financial statement presentation at each reporting date.
• Reconcile investments capturing purchases, maturities, disposals, gains/losses, accrued interest, and impairment (ASC 326); apply mark-to-market or amortized cost as applicable.
• Support investment-related disclosure requirements in quarterly and annual mock SEC filings (10-Q and 10-K), working closely with the Financial Reporting team.

Derivative Instruments
• Run the quarterly mark-to-market valuation model (ASC 815, ASC 820) — refreshing scenario-based assumptions and market inputs (third-party fair value quotes and interest rates) each quarter and recording the quarter-over-quarter change in fair value; reconcile derivative balances, document valuations, and support audit and disclosure requirements.
• Monitor embedded features for bifurcation assessment (ASC 815); maintain a documented trigger-assessment process ahead of each close.
• Treasury Accounting Review & Analytics
• Review accounting activities — including bank account reconciliations, cash journal entries, and other financial instrument-related balance sheet accounts — for accuracy, completeness, and proper US GAAP treatment
• Proactively monitor and assess accounting impact of new and evolving accounting standards and any new, modified, or newly settled financial instruments or transactions; ensuring a documented plan and conclusion is in place before the reporting date.
• Read and interpret the underlying contractual terms of debt, investment, trust, and cash arrangements, and partner cross-functionally with Treasury, Legal and the business to reach and document well-supported accounting conclusions.
• Prepare monthly and quarterly treasury accounting analytics — including variance analyses, trend reporting, and clear management summaries — to support internal reporting and management review.
• Ensure full coverage of all financial instruments and related cash matters — including bank and trust / GCP (customer funds held in trust) account activity unusual or aged reconciling items.
• Account for and reconcile customer trust / GCP balances in accordance with the applicable US GAAP presentation and any contractual or regulatory safeguarding requirements.
• Own SOX controls across all financial-instrument processes — performing and evidencing key controls, keeping process and control documentation current, and partnering with internal and external audit on walkthroughs and testing.

AI & Automation
• Build & scale — applying AI platforms including Glean and Claude to automate financial instrument workflows, documenting/sharing via the use-case library, and driving the roadmap with peers/leadership.
• Agent governance — designing and orchestrating AI agents with guardrails and human-in-the-loop review, staying fully accountable for output.
• Product rigor & controls — treating automations as documented, version-controlled, SOX-compliant products with measurable outcomes tracked.
• Continuous improvement & change management — optimizing/redesigning processes, leading adoption and training, and staying current on industry-leading AI practices.

What You'll Need to be Successful

Must Have
• CA, CPA, or MBA (Finance) — US CPA strongly preferred
• 5+ years in financial instruments, treasury, or technical accounting
• Deep, hands-on US GAAP expertise across financial instruments and public-company-style disclosures
• Proven track record of automating manual accounting work
• Proficiency with AI platforms (Glean, ChatGPT, Claude), SQL/Python, and ERP/EPM systems (NetSuite, Oracle, Workday, SAP)
• Highly detail-oriented with meticulous ownership of quality; genuinely AI-curious; a collaborative team player who steps up when needed and helps upskill teammates

Good to Have
• Big 4 or equivalent public accounting experience (strongly preferred)
• Background in SaaS or technology industry
• Experience with treasury / reconciliation tools such as Kyriba
• Experience building a team-wide AI use-case library and scaling automation roadmaps

Avalara is an AI-first Company

AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products. Success here requires embracing AI as an essential capability.
• You’ll bring experience using AI and AI-related technologies, ready to thrive here.
• You’ll apply AI every day to business challenges - improving efficiency, contributing solutions, and driving results for your team, our company, and our customers.
• You’ll grow with AI by staying curious about new trends and best practices, and by sharing what you learn so others can benefit too.

How We'll Take Care of You

Total Rewards

In addition to a great compensation package, paid time off, and paid parental leave, many Avalara employees are eligible for bonuses.

Health & Wellness
Benefits vary by location but generally include private medical, life, and disability insurance.

Inclusive culture and diversity
Avalara strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion, and is committed to integrating them into our business practices and our organizational culture. We also have a total of 8 employee-run resource groups, each with senior leadership and exec sponsorship.

We’ve already built an industry-leading cloud compliance platform, processing over 54 billion customer API calls and over 6.6 million tax returns a year. Our growth is real - we're a billion dollar business - and we’re not slowing down until we’ve achieved our mission - to be part of every transaction in the world.
